newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FABREGAS HOMER IN 11TH HELPS WHITE SOX BEAT RED SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FABREGAS HOMER IN 11TH HELPS WHITE SOX BEAT RED SOX.

text.p: Jorge Fabregas's first homer of the season, a two-run shot in the top of the 11th, highlighted a four-run outburst as the Chicago White Sox defeated the Boston Red Sox 5-2 Thursday.

Fabregas, acquired from the Angels earlier this month, hit a 3-1 pitch from reliever John Wasdin (0-3) over the right-field wall to snap a 1-1 tie. Ray Durham added a two-run single later in the frame to push the lead to 5-1.

"I got lucky," said Fabergas. "He threw a fastball that was up. I took advantage of it. I was thinking maybe with first base open, they might go ahead and pitch to me a little Boston got back a run in the bottom of the 11th on a sacrifice fly by Jeff Frye but Bill Simas came on to record the final out for his first save since September 14.

The Red Sox rallied to knot the game with two out in the bottom of the ninth when Mo Vaughn homered off Chicago closer Roberto Hernandez (3-1). Vaughn had been 0-for-13 with eight strikeouts against Hernandez.
"Regardless of the situation, it was the first base hit off me for Mo," said Hernandez. "I can live with the fact that it was Mo and nobody else. It was a situation where I'm not going to back away."
Boston then put runners on first and third before Hernandez struck out Troy O'Leary, sending the game to extra innings.

"It was a good baseball game," said Red Sox third baseman Tim Naehring, who had two hits. "Everyone who came to the park saw a good game. We played well and they played well. Mo came up with a big knock and we were just one hit away from winning it in the ninth."
Overshadowed was the performance of White Sox starter Danny Darwin, who allowed just two hits over eight scoreless innings.
Albert Belle doubled in the fourth inning to extend his hitting streak to a career-high 24 games. The streak is the longest in the major leagues this season, equalled later by Seattle's Joey Cora.
In Seattle, Juan Gonzalez and Ivan Rodriguez homered and a throwing error by third baseman Brent Gates sparked a five-run seventh inning as the Texas Rangers defeated the Mariners 8-2.

Rodriguez homered in the first off starter Jamie Moyer (4-2) and Gonzalez hit a solo shot in the fourth to knot the game at 2-2. Mike Devereaux's RBI single in the sixth put the Rangers on top for good before the five-run seventh put the game out of reach.
Ken Hill (4-2) allowed two unearned runs and six hits in seven innings. His third straight win was just the Rangers' fourth in their last 25 games at Seattle.
Cora beat out an infield single on an 0-2 pitch in his final at-bat in the ninth to extend his hitting streak to 24, longest by a switch-hitter in American League history.
In Toronto, David Cone and Jeff Nelson combined on a five-hitter with 15 strikeouts as the New York Yankees completed a two-game sweep of the Blue Jays, 4-0.

Tino Martinez hit his 20th homer and drove in two runs for the Yankees, who have won two straight after losing seven of eight. Luis Sojo drove in the other two runs for the Yankees, who played in front of Toronto's largest crowd of the season -- 43,155.
Cone (6-3) allowed all five hits and walked one, matching his season high with 12 strikeouts in 7 2/3 innings in his first win as a visitor to Toronto.

Nelson picked up his first save by striking out the first three batters he faced and retiring Ruben Sierra on a groundout to end the game. He struck out Joe Carter with two on after relieving Cone in the eighth en route to his first save since May 7 of last season.
Woody Williams (1-5) gave up all four runs.

In Oakland, Allen Watson allowed one run over seven innings in his second straight solid outing and Gary DiSarcina and Garret Anderson each drove in two runs to lead the surging Anaheim Angels to a 7-1 romp over the Athletics.
The Angels have won 13 of their last 17 games and completed a 4-3 road trip.
At Minnesota, Jeromy Burnitz had a two-run double and Mark Loretta hit a two-run homer as the Milwaukee Brewers stopped a three-game losing streak with a 7-4 win over the Twins.

Two games were postponed due to rain. In Detroit, the Baltimore Orioles and Tigers were rescheduled as part of a doubleheader on July 4, and in Kansas City, the Cleveland Indians and Royals were rescheduled as part of a doubleheader on September 19.
